token_needed: This meshctl asks for an access token to use its radios.
token_wrong: That is not the token this meshctl asks for.
token_hint: It is the MESHCTL_TOKEN meshctl was started with. This browser will remember it.
token_unreachable: It could not be checked: meshctl does not answer.
welcome_lead: Your Meshtastic and MeshCore radios in one place: their nodes on the map, the messages, what goes through the mesh and their settings.
welcome_more: You can add more later, of both kinds, and switch between them whenever you like.
welcome_usb_detail: Plugged into the computer meshctl runs on
welcome_address_hint: Its IP or its name on the network. With :port at the end if it does not use {port}.
welcome_device_hint: With @speed at the end if it does not run at 115200.
welcome_name_hint: Leave it empty to take the radio's own.
welcome_step_sync: Receive its settings and its nodes
welcome_failed: The radio does not answer at {address}.
welcome_failed_hint: Check that it is on and that the address is its own. meshctl keeps trying on its own.
meshcore_companion: A MeshCore companion answers next to nothing: only a route search, and only if it shares its base telemetry, which is off out of the box.
settings_not_connected: The radio is not connected. Its settings are read from it, and changed in it, only while it is.
settings_reboot_hint: Any change on this tab reboots the radio: it drops its link for a moment.
section_invalid: The radio does not take one of those values: check the limits of the fields changed.
settings_reboot_confirm: These changes reboot the radio, which drops its link for a moment. Go ahead?
settings_applied: Sent to the radio. They are read back from it in a few seconds.
settings_applied_reboot: Sent to the radio, which is rebooting to apply them. meshctl reconnects on its own.
settings_invalid: The radio does not take those settings: check the values changed.
settings_no_answer: The radio did not answer. Nothing was changed.
chat_pick: Pick a channel or a node to talk to.
chat_reply_unknown: A message that is not here
chat_delete_confirm: Delete this message? It is only deleted from meshctl: what went out on the mesh cannot be taken back.
link_key: It brings its public key: you can write to it privately.
link_no_key: It does not bring its public key: you cannot write to it privately until its node info is heard.
link_known: The radio knows it already: it is brought up to date with what the link has.
link_nothing: The radio has all of these channels already.
link_channels_fit: {n} will be added to the free slots; there are {free}.
link_channels_full: They do not fit: they take {n} slots and there are {free}.
link_lora_differs: These channels are on {preset}, which is not what your radio uses: only those on those settings will hear them. Adding them leaves your LoRa as it is.
link_invalid: It is not a Meshtastic contact or channels link.
link_no_slots: The radio has no free slots for these channels.
link_refused: The radio did not take it.
link_hint_node: A node's contact link, as the {apps} apps share it. Nothing is added until you confirm.
link_hint_channels: A channels link, as the {apps} apps share it. Nothing changes until you confirm.
link_for_channels: It is a channels link: channels are added from Settings → Channels.
link_for_nodes: It is a contact link: it is added from the list of nodes.
link_replaces: It is a whole configuration: whoever shares it means it to replace your channels. You can add them to yours or replace them.
link_replace_summary: Your radio will keep only these {n} channels; the first will be the primary.
link_lora_warning: The radio reboots and hears only those on those settings. Unticked, your LoRa stays as it is.
chat_sending: Sending: the radio does not have it yet
chat_sent: Sent: the radio put it out, nobody known to have heard it yet
chat_on_its_way: On its way: a node passed it on, the one it goes to has yet to confirm it
chat_got: Got: the radio heard another node pass it on
chat_nobody: Nobody heard it: it can be sent again
chat_delivered: Delivered: the node said it got it
chat_not_connected: The radio is not connected: you can read, not send.
chat_unkept: The radio does not keep this node: MeshCore writes only to its contacts.
chat_unkept_short: Add it to the radio to write to it
chat_invalid: That message cannot be sent: it is empty or too long, or the channel is not on the radio.
chat_muted: Silenced: not counted as unread, nor notified of.
chat_position_nowhere: The radio does not know where it is
chat_position_confirm: Send where the radio is to this conversation? It goes {how}, as the channel shares positions.
radio_address_hint: On the network: host or host:port (4403 for Meshtastic and 5000 for MeshCore when none is given). Over USB: the device's path, such as /dev/ttyACM0, with @speed if it is not 115200.
radio_remove_confirm: Remove this radio? meshctl will disconnect from it and forget what it heard.
radio_last_connected: What you see is what it knew when it was last connected, {{ ago }} ago.
offline_daemon_short: What you see is the last that was known; the page keeps trying on its own.
offline_disabled_short: meshctl does not connect to it.
offline_node: What it answered before can be read, but nothing new can be asked of it.
offline_disabled_text: meshctl does not connect to it. Turn it on to see its nodes and what it hears.
offline_unreachable_text: meshctl keeps trying. As soon as it reaches it, what it hears will be here.
error_invalid_name: Give the radio a name, of up to 64 characters.
error_invalid_address: That is not an address meshctl understands.
error_unsupported_kind: This meshctl cannot talk to that kind of radio yet.
error_failed: meshctl could not do it. Try again.
room_sending: Sending the login to the room
room_waiting: Waiting for the room to answer
room_log_in_again: Log in again, if messages stop coming
room_why_out: The room only sends its messages to those logged in. With no password you log in as a guest, if the room allows it.
room_why_read_only: You are logged in to read only. To write, log in with the room's password.
room_wrong_password: The room did not take the password.
room_no_answer: The room did not answer: it may be far off, or take neither the password nor guests.
room_failed: Could not log in to the room.
room_gone_short: The radio does not find this room among its contacts.
room_gone_title: The radio does not find this room
room_gone_text: The radio does not find it among its contacts: meshctl remembers it from when it was heard, or something in between, such as a splitter, still lists it. It cannot be logged in to until the radio hears it advertise again. Remove it for good? The radio forgets it, if it still lists it, and meshctl deletes what it keeps of it, its messages included.
room_forget_sure: Forget the password kept for this room? It will have to be typed next time.
own_contact_qr: QR code of this radio's contact
own_contact_hint_meshtastic: Scan it with the Meshtastic app to add this radio as a contact, with its key. Or share the link.
own_contact_hint_meshcore: Scan it with the MeshCore app to add this radio as a contact. Or share the link.
node_contact_hint_meshtastic: Scan it with the Meshtastic app to add this node as a contact, with its key. Or share the link.
node_contact_hint_meshcore: Scan it with the MeshCore app to add this node as a contact. Or share the link.
node_contact_none: It cannot be shared yet: its public key is missing, which comes with its node info.
remove_radio_text: The radio forgets it. meshctl still shows it in the list, marked as kept here only, with its history: heard again, it is back on the radio.
remove_all_text: The radio forgets it and meshctl deletes all it keeps of it: requests, traceroutes, the direct conversation and all its packets, its metrics with them. Its messages in channels stay.
remove_refused: The radio would not forget it; nothing was deleted.
remove_no_answer: The radio did not answer; nothing was deleted.
packets_empty: Nothing heard yet: packets show here as the radio hears them.
packets_none: No packet gets through these filters.
packets_relay_unknown: Not told: the node that relayed it does not say
packets_relay_guess: Guessed: it may be another node with the hash {hash}
packets_trace_hint: The route asked for by whoever sent it, hop by hop, and the SNR each repeater heard it at as it went through.
node_not_connected: The radio is not connected: what the node answered before can be read, nothing new asked.
ask_login_no_answer: Not asked: it has to log in to the node first, and the node did not let it in with no password. It may be far, or have a guest password; if you know it, type it under «Access».
ask_login_refused: Not asked: the node did not let it in with no password.
ask_too_soon: That is still waiting for its answer, or the radio sent the like a moment ago.
ask_invalid_channel: The radio does not use that channel.
map_empty: None of this radio's nodes has said where it is yet.
map_route_none: {{ name }} did not answer the traceroute
radios_count: {{ count }} radios · in this order on the rail
radios_count_phone: {{ count }} radios · in this order in the list
radios_hint: Drag a row by its handle, or use its arrows, to move it on the rail. The eye shows or hides it on the rail; the switch is “Connect automatically”: turning it off disconnects it right away. A hidden radio stays here, ready to come back.
radios_hint_phone: Use its arrows to move it in the list of radios. The eye shows or hides it in that list; the switch is “Connect automatically”: turning it off disconnects it right away. A hidden radio stays here, ready to come back.
radio_drag: Drag to move it on the rail
radio_enabled_hint: It connects when meshctl starts and again whenever the link is lost. Turning it off disconnects it right away.
radio_shown_hint: Hidden, it stays set up here.
radio_look_text_hint: Up to four letters, or one emoji, as Meshtastic's short names. Empty, the node's short name, or the initials if it has none.
error_invalid_badge: That button will not do: the colour must be #rrggbb, the text up to four letters or one emoji, and the emoji an emoji.
emoji_failed: The emojis could not be loaded.
prefs_map_hint: The map's, apart from the panel's.
prefs_language_hint: The one meshctl speaks to you in.
prefs_accent_hint: The buttons', what is picked, and focus.
settings_long_name_hint: The one others in the mesh see you by.
settings_short_name_hint: Up to four letters, or one emoji: the one on the map.
settings_role_hint: What the radio does in the mesh. Changing it reboots it.
settings_region_hint: Sets the frequencies it transmits on: those of where you are.
settings_use_preset_hint: A ready-made profile of range and speed. Without one, they are set by hand; all nodes that talk must match.
settings_preset_hint: Nodes that are to talk to each other must use the same one.
settings_hop_limit_hint: How many times what you send may be relayed, 1 to 7.
channels_hint: Each channel is saved to the radio as it is saved here.
channel_key_custom_hint: In base64, as the apps show it: of 16 or 32 bytes.
channel_key_default_hint: Everyone knows it: what is sent on the channel is not private.
channel_key_none_hint: What is sent on the channel goes unencrypted.
channel_uplink_hint: What it hears on this channel is published on the radio's MQTT server.
channel_downlink_hint: What comes from the MQTT server is sent out on this channel.
channel_invalid: The radio does not take that channel: check its name and, if your own, its key.
channel_primary_confirm: will become the primary channel: the radio sends its position and its node's info on it. Go on?
channel_remove_question: It goes off the radio, its key with it, and those after it move up a slot. And its messages? Kept, they are not in the chat, but they come back if you add the very same channel again (name and key).
channel_duplicate: There already is a channel with that name and key: to the radio they would be the same, and all that is heard would go to the first. Change the name or the key.
channel_position_hint: The radio sends its position on this channel, as precisely as you choose.
channel_public_hint: It is a public channel: the radio sends the position no more precisely than this.
channel_public_precision: It is a public channel: the radio sends the position no more precisely than ± 730 m. Choose less precision, or a key of your own.
channel_muted_hint: As its chat's bell: not counted as unread nor notified of, here, on the radio and in the Meshtastic apps.
settings_bandwidth_hint: Wider is faster, and reaches less far.
settings_spread_factor_hint: Higher reaches farther, and is slower: each packet takes longer on the air.
settings_coding_rate_hint: More redundancy stands a weaker signal, but makes each packet longer.
settings_tx_power_hint: In dBm. 0 is the most the region allows:
settings_slot_hint: Empty, the radio picks it by the primary channel's name (auto). Slots in this region at this bandwidth:
settings_frequency_hint: Empty, the slot's (auto). The region's band:
settings_offset_hint: Added to the frequency, to make up for an off crystal. Only with test equipment.
settings_duty_hint: Only if your licence lets you: the limit is the law's. In this region,
settings_boosted_hint: On SX126x radios, hears better for a little more power.
settings_ok_mqtt_hint: Lets others' gateways put what you send on the internet.
settings_ignore_mqtt_hint: Leaves aside what other nodes relay from the internet.
settings_fan_hint: Only on boards that have one.
settings_advanced_hint: Power, frequency, duty cycle and MQTT: what few need to touch.
settings_status_hint: What the radio tells of how it is, now and then. Empty, nothing.
settings_unmessagable_hint: Tells others nobody reads messages here: for nodes of the mesh's own.
settings_licensed_hint: Lets it past its region's power and band, but the radio sends nothing encrypted, as the licence has it. The long name should be your call sign.
empty_disabled_text: meshctl does not connect to it, and its settings are read from the radio itself. Switch it on to see them.
empty_offline_text: Its settings are read from the radio and changed on it, only while it is connected. meshctl keeps trying.
empty_daemon_text: meshctl's service cannot be reached. The page tries again by itself every few seconds.
mark_routed: With a known route of {n} hops: what is sent to it goes along it
mark_routed_one: With a known route of 1 hop: what is sent to it goes along it
mark_no_route: No known route: the next thing sent to it floods the mesh to find one
check_shared_text: Its public key is the same as that of other nodes heard in the latest week: {nodes}. Each of them can read what is sent to the others alone. It happens with radios that came with the same key, or whose settings were copied from another: making a new key on this node ends it.
check_conflict_text: Its latest node info carries {n} different public keys. Either two radios share its id, or the key was made anew, as when it is reflashed: until the others take the new one, what is sent to it fails.
check_hardware_text: Its latest node info names more than one hardware model: {models}. Either two radios share its id, or the radio was replaced.
node_quiet: It answered {ago} ago: it will not answer again for {left}.
node_pace_position: The radio can send positions again in {n} s.
node_pace_telemetry: The radio can send telemetry again in {n} s.
node_pace_traceroute: The radio can trace another route in {n} s.
node_mqtt_hint: Heard through MQTT only: requests may not reach it.
node_sensors_hint: It answers only with the sensors, or the module on.
node_sensors_own_hint: Only those it has on, or that have told something, are shown.
node_unknown: Its name, hardware and public key are not known yet, and without its key it cannot be asked for telemetry or neighbours: its node info brings all of them.
node_channel_menu: On the channel (the node has to have it too)
node_direct_pki: Encrypted to its public key, whatever the channel
node_direct_meshcore: Encrypted end to end, with a key only the two radios share
node_direct_licensed: On the channel: your radio is licensed, nothing goes encrypted
traces_none: No route to it traced yet.
traces_meshcore_hint: It is traced along the route the radio keeps, there and back: one of a hop at least is needed. One heard straight is better pinged.
traces_repeat_hint: It answers only when set to repeat, which rooms and sensors are not out of the box.
trace_guess_hint: Underlined repeaters are guessed by how near and within reach they are, not known for sure.
node_no_key: Its public key is not known, and without it it cannot be asked for telemetry or neighbours: its node info brings it, if its firmware has one.
node_needs_key: Its public key is needed, which its node info brings: without it the radio does not send this.
node_direct_none: Nothing, until its key is known: the radio encrypts to it what is for it alone
node_kept: Only in meshctl: the radio does not have it in its list
node_kept_hint: The radio does not have it in its list: only meshctl keeps it. Heard again, it is back on the radio.
node_kept_meshcore: Not among the radio's contacts: it heard it advertise and did not add it, or it was removed. Add it to write to it and have the radio keep it.
chat_unmessagable: This node tells that nobody reads its messages; it is usually a repeater or a sensor. You can write to it, but most likely nobody will read it.
chart_nothing: Nothing to show over this while.
request_timeout: nothing in two minutes; it may have answered lately
request_ping_timeout: it did not come back in time
request_due_timeout: it did not answer in time
request_no_key: the radio did not send it: its public key is missing
forget_requests_sure: Delete all its requests? What the node told stays on its page.
forget_traces_sure: Delete the earlier traceroutes? The latest stays on the page.
data_text: What meshctl keeps, and for how long
data_packets_hint: What the live view, the charts and the details of messages and requests show. Each node's latest of each kind is always kept, however old.
data_nodes_hint: Those the radio no longer has, not heard for so long. Never a favourite. Their conversations stay.
data_messages_hint: In channels and direct. Unless cleaned, they are kept for ever.
data_daily: meshctl cleans on its own when it starts, once a day and when a time changes.
data_cleaned: {packets} packets, {nodes} nodes and {messages} messages cleaned; {bytes} freed.
data_gone_count: Conversations: {conversations} · messages: {messages}. They go for good.
newer_text: This tab still runs the one before: reload it to use the new one.
mc_name_hint: What it advertises itself as, and others see. Up to 31 bytes.
mc_position_hint: Where it says it is, in degrees. Empty, nowhere. Its adverts carry it only if it shares it (in Advanced).
mc_gps_hint: The radio's own: on, it says where the radio is, instead of what is written below, and takes more battery.
mc_position_gps: Its GPS says it, while it is on. Its adverts carry it only if it shares it (in Advanced).
position_pick_hint: Tap the map, or drag the pin
position_here_asking: Asking this device where it is…
position_here_denied: This device was not allowed to say where it is. You can allow it in its settings or the browser's.
position_here_failed: This device could not tell where it is.
position_here_insecure: Only over HTTPS, or in the app, can this device be asked where it is.
position_fixed_hint: In degrees, and the altitude in metres if you want. As it says now until you change it.
position_applied: The radio says it is there now.
mc_frequency_hint: In MHz. It hears only those on the same, with the same modulation.
mc_bandwidth_hint: Narrower reaches further, but each message takes longer to go out.
mc_sf_hint: Higher reaches further, but each message takes longer on the air.
mc_cr_hint: How much of each message goes to correcting errors: more, sturdier and longer.
mc_tx_power_hint: In dBm, from −9 to {max}, the most this board gives.
mc_repeat_hint: Repeats what it hears, like a repeater. Only on {frequencies} MHz.
mc_manual_add_hint: Nodes that advertise do not join its contacts by themselves, but for the kinds you tick.
mc_share_position_hint: Its adverts say where it is, and put it on others' maps.
mc_telemetry_base_hint: Who it answers with its battery and state.
mc_telemetry_location_hint: Who it answers, if asked, with where it is.
mc_telemetry_environment_hint: Who it answers with what its sensors measure.
mc_multi_acks_hint: It sends each acknowledgement more than once: they arrive better, at the cost of more time on the air.
mc_radio_confirm: On another frequency or modulation, the radio will hear only those on the same. Sure?
mc_applied: Saved: the radio uses it now.
mc_channels_hint: Each channel is saved on the radio as it is saved here. Channels by name take their key from the name itself: anyone who knows it hears them.
mc_channel_name_hint: Write it with a # in front, like #galicia, for a channel by name: its key comes from the name, as in the MeshCore apps. The radio keeps it without the #.
mc_secret_hashtag: The key comes from the name: anyone who knows it can hear the channel.
mc_channel_invalid: The radio does not take that channel: check the name (up to 31 bytes) and the key.
mc_channel_share_hint: Scan it with the MeshCore app to add the channel. Or share the link: it carries its key.
mc_channel_remove_question: Remove the channel from the radio? Its conversation stays in meshctl.
mc_path_none: None: what is sent to it floods to find one
mc_path_hint: If the path stops working, reset it: the next message floods and finds a new one. Nothing is sent now.
mc_path_not_contact: Not one of the radio's contacts: it keeps no path to it.
mc_route_hint: Asking for it floods the mesh for the route to it and back, hop by hop: it goes on the air, and the radio keeps the one it has. Only a node that shares its base telemetry answers, which companions do not out of the box, or a repeater, room or sensor that can be logged in to.
mc_route_lost: It did not answer the last route search.
mc_advert_hint: The radio says who it is, for others to add it as a contact: nearby, to the nodes that hear it directly; or to the whole mesh, through the repeaters.
mc_advert_sent_flood: Advert sent to the whole mesh.
mc_scope_hint: What it floods is passed on only by that region's repeaters, like #galicia. Empty, it reaches the whole mesh.
mc_autoadd_kinds_hint: Even with contacts added by hand, the kinds of node that join them by themselves as they advertise.
mc_autoadd_hops_hint: Up to how many hops away nodes that advertise are added by themselves.
mc_overwrite_hint: With the contact list full, a new one takes the place of the oldest that is not a favourite.
mc_hash_hint: What each hop takes in the path of what it sends. More bytes tell repeaters apart better, at the cost of longer packets.
mc_rx_delay_hint: The base of the wait before handling what reaches it flooded, 0 to 20. 0 for none.
mc_airtime_hint: How much of the air it leaves free after sending, against what it took, 0 to 9.
mc_reorder_failed: The radio did not take the new order; the channels are back as they were.
access_list_none: Not asked yet who may log in.
console_hint: Commands go to the node's console, as in its CLI: ver, clock, get name, neighbors…
console_hint_own: Commands go to the radio's own console, as in its CLI: ver, board, get name, set name…
console_risky: “{command}” may leave the node out of service or out of reach. Send it?
console_not_admin: Only its admin may use the console: log in with its password.
remote_status_none: Not asked yet. Asking logs in as a guest first, if needed.
remote_telemetry_hint: A guest is told its own only; its sensors, its admin.
series_none: Not asked yet. Asking logs in first, if need be.
series_empty: it kept nothing of that time.
series_lost: The last request got no answer.
series_hint: What the sensor kept of its readings over that time: the lowest, the mean and the highest. Its stock firmware keeps its battery voltage alone; one of its own may keep more.
remote_neighbors_none: Not asked yet whom it hears straight.
ping_lost: The last ping did not come back.
ping_only_direct: No longer heard straight: only nodes the radio hears straight can be pinged again.
access_entering: Logging in with no password… {s} s
access_no_answer: It did not answer: it may be far off, or not take the password.
access_hint: With no password you log in as a guest, if the node allows it. What it is asked logs in first, if needed.
regions_none: Not asked yet. It answers only if the request reaches it direct.
regions_nothing: It repeats nothing, with a region or without.
regions_hint: What is flooded it passes on only in one of these regions; with “No region”, when it carries none.
ask_no_path: No path to it is known, and these requests go only direct: wait to hear an advert from it.
regions_nearby_hint: Asks the repeaters it knows a path to, up to two hops, which regions they repeat. Click one to use it by default; the figure says how many repeat it straight, of those that answered.
regions_unserved: No repeater it hears straight repeats #{name}: what it floods will not go past its reach.
regions_unscoped_unserved: No repeater it hears straight repeats with no region: what it floods with none will not go past its reach.
mc_channel_scope_hint: The region what you send to this channel floods in. The radio does not keep it: meshctl does, and it goes in its link.
mc_channel_scope_menu: Region what you send to this channel floods in
regions_subtitle_unserved: No repeater the radio hears straight repeats this region: what you send will not go past its reach.
route_hint: Each copy that came and which way: the repeaters from its sender's side to this radio.
route_echoes_hint: The copies of your message this radio heard as it was repeated, and which way.
route_unknown: A repeater this radio does not know
route_guess: Guessed among {n} possible with the hash {hash}, by the route: it may be another
route_guess_only: Guessed: the only known node with the hash {hash}, but it may be another this radio does not know
route_misfit: {n} known with the hash {hash}, but none fits the route: likely another this radio does not know
route_guess_hint: Repeaters with a dashed border are guessed by how near and within reach they are, not known for sure.
route_unplaced: Not enough of this route's nodes have a known position to show it on the map.
chat_unheard: No repeater heard it: it can be sent again
chat_waiting_repeaters: Sent: waiting to hear a repeater pass it on
chat_reaction_orphan: reacted to a message not here
qr_photo: or read it from a photo
qr_camera_hint: Frame the QR and it reads by itself
qr_no_camera: The browser only allows the live camera over HTTPS.
qr_not_found: No QR found in the photo.
qr_photo_pick: Pick or take a photo of the QR
link_hint_lora: A configuration link, as the Meshtastic apps share it. Only its LoRa is taken: into the form, for you to look over and save.
link_lora_will_change: It is not what your radio uses: once saved, the radio restarts and only hears those on these settings.
link_lora_same: Its region and modem are what your radio already uses.
link_no_lora: This link brings only channels, no LoRa.
link_for_lora: It is a contact link: it is added from the list of nodes.
about_text: meshctl is a control panel for your mesh radios, Meshtastic and MeshCore: it connects to them over the network or a cable and lets you talk on their channels and in private, see their nodes on the map, follow the packets they hear and set them up.
about_license: Free software under the GPL, version 3 or later
replies_text: What meshctl answers on its own, and where
notifications_text: What meshctl lets you know of as it hears it
notifications_on_hint: Where you say below; never of the conversation you have in front of you.
notifications_browser_granted: In this browser, while meshctl is open in some tab.
notifications_browser_ask: This browser has to let meshctl show them.
notifications_browser_denied: This browser blocks them for meshctl: they are allowed in the site's settings.
notifications_browser_unsupported: This browser cannot show them here: they usually need meshctl over HTTPS.
notifications_status_app: This app shows them, with its window closed too.
notifications_sample_text: Anyone around A Coruña this evening? 📡
notifications_where_hint: Of what each radio hears. Mentions: only when someone writes @ and its name on the mesh.
notifications_look_hint: With what the message says, or only who wrote it and where.
replies_empty_text: meshctl can answer a message on its own, even with the panel closed: a ping, say, with the hops it took and its signal. If someone writes this, answer with that.
replies_hint: A message is answered by the first that fits it: drag a row by its handle, or use its arrows, to change the order. The switch turns one off everywhere, keeping where it answers.
replies_hint_phone: A message is answered by the first that fits it: use the arrows to change the order. The switch turns one off everywhere, keeping where it answers.
reply_match_whole_hint: Separated by commas. The message is one of them, whatever its case, accents, punctuation or emojis: “Ping!” is ping, “ping me” is not.
reply_match_word_hint: Separated by commas. The message has one of them among its words, whatever its case, accents or punctuation: “a ping, please” has ping, “pinging” has not.
reply_direct: Another text if it came direct
reply_direct_hint: Only direct is the signal the sender's own: with hops, it is the last repeater's.
reply_over: Past 200 bytes: what goes beyond is cut.
reply_variables_hint: Tap one to put it in the text; each takes its value from the message answered, and one it does not carry is left empty. The example is Ana, three hops away, or direct.
reply_meshcore_note: On MeshCore, no short name or RSSI comes, and the SNR is always the last hop's.
reply_where_hint: On each radio, where it listens and answers. Channels are followed wherever they go on the radio.
reply_no_channels: Its channels show once it is connected.
reply_enabled_hint: Off, it answers nowhere, and keeps where it would.
reply_var_long_name: Who wrote it, by their long name
reply_var_short_name: Who wrote it, by their short name
reply_var_node_id: Who wrote it, by their node's id
reply_var_hops: The hops it took, as a number
reply_var_kangaroo_hops: The hops it took, as kangaroos
error_invalid_auto_reply: It needs a name, something to wait for, and something to answer with, its texts up to 200 bytes.
replies_busy_hint: None answers on a radio that hears its channel busy more of the time than this. Until it has said how busy, it answers.
reply_sign_hint: Before the text, unless it starts so: an automatic reply is told apart so, and other bots do not answer it.
app_background: Keep listening with the app closed
app_background_hint: The radios stay connected, automatic replies answer and notifications reach you. Off, closing meshctl ends it, and it listens only while you use it.
plugged_asked: Android is asking you for leave to use it: say yes.
plugged_none: No radio plugged in. Plug it in and it will show here.
plugged_pick: Pick it from those plugged in
radio_add_name_hint: Without one, the one plugged in's, or its address.
radio_add_customize_hint: Its icon or letters, and its colour on the bar, right after adding it.
nearby_asked: Android is asking you for leave to use Bluetooth: say yes, and look again.
nearby_none: No radio heard nearby. Is its Bluetooth on, and that of this device?
